plain: We could not follow it from year to year: in single WISE epochs it is too faint or sits on other stars, so its motion is not measured here. Stacking all WISE images along its catalog motion (0.36 arcseconds per year) does show it (signal-to-noise 17), so it is there, just too faint to follow year by year.
Its infrared colour W1-W2 = 2.56 mag is very red, like T-type brown dwarfs.
Its infrared brightness stays constant within the measurement errors.
Not enough clean SPHEREx measurements to read its spectrum.
